espn-604005.headline: From Cardiff to the side that beat them last November
beats: New Zealand's 35–28 defeat in Cardiff last weekend was their first loss to Wales for 73 years. The last time they met England, on 15 November 2025, England won 33–19 at home.
Dave Rennie has made eight changes and handed the captaincy back to Codie Taylor. Beauden Barrett plays at fullback and wins his 150th Test cap, only the fourth player to get there.
England arrive on four straight wins, the last a 78–15 win over Japan with 13 tries. Steve Borthwick still made nine changes, and Henry Pollock drops to the bench.
A bonus-point win puts New Zealand into next Sunday's final, at South Africa's expense. A second straight defeat to England would earn them a different kind of week.

espn-604006.headline: Japan let in 78 last week. Scotland pick a new XV
beats: Injuries, captain Sione Tuipulotu among them, plus heavy rotation have rebuilt the side that beat Australia 15–12. Newcastle No 8 Ollie Leatherbarrow makes his first Scotland start.
Japan lost 78–15 to England, a record defeat, a week after going down 21–28 in Wales. The last time they played Scotland in Edinburgh, the hosts won 29–20.
Any Japan win would lift them above Italy in the world rankings. Italy are Scotland's next opponents, at home in February.
Eddie Jones, Japan's coach, says Gregor Townsend has 'done a great job'. Generous, from a man whose side have won one of five in the competition.

espn-604007.headline: The world's No 1 side, coached by watch-along
beats: Rassie Erasmus has a six-match ban for questioning the integrity of match officials, his third for criticising referees. Barred from Lansdowne Road, he has invited fans to join him in an online watch-along instead.

Ireland are improvising too. With Caelan Doris and two others injured, Dan Sheehan, the captain and a hooker, starts at No 8. His only previous start there was for Leinster on this ground last month, when they badly lost the breakdown and still won.
Sam Prendergast plays at fly-half after his hip-drop citing was dismissed. Erasmus had predicted that.
South Africa won 24–13 in Dublin last November, then lost 21–19 in France a week ago. Any Ireland win ends their time at No 1, and their coach will be reviewing it online like everyone else.

espn-604008.headline: Beaten by Argentina, Italy turn to Argentina's old 10
beats: Domingo Miotti, the Montpellier fly-half who used to play for Argentina, makes his Italy debut against Fiji in Udine. He replaces Paolo Garbisi, who started the 14–19 defeat by Argentina on 14 November.

That five-point loss is the closest Italy have come in six straight defeats. The week before it, South Africa put 66 on them. Fiji have their own leak: 54 and 43 conceded in a fortnight, at France and Ireland.
Both sides are winless after five rounds, so the loser finishes the pool stage bottom of all twelve. Win, and Italy also pass Fiji into 10th in the world.
Italy lost by five to the country Miotti used to play for. Against Fiji, a win by five would do nicely.

espn-604009.headline: Two months out, Jalibert walks straight into the No 10 shirt
beats: Matthieu Jalibert has not played since September, when a thigh injury put him out for two months. With Thomas Ramos and Romain Ntamack both unavailable, he starts at fly-half beside Antoine Dupont, and Kalvin Gourgues is expected to take the kicks. Fabien Galthié's position is that if he plays, he is fit.

France have won four straight, the last 21–19 over South Africa, and sit a point ahead of England at the top of the North conference with the Grand final place at stake. Even a draw drops them to fourth in the world, below Ireland.
Argentina beat Italy 19–14 a week after conceding 42 in Ireland, and Midi Olympique found little to admire in Rome. Julián Montoya is back as captain, one of seven changes.
Seven of that Argentina starting XV play in the Top 14. Jalibert will at least be facing people who know exactly what he looks like at full speed.

espn-604010.headline: Wales beat the side that put 93 on Australia
beats: Wales scored five tries past New Zealand in Cardiff on 14 November and won 35–28. In October, New Zealand beat Australia 50–19 and 43–21.

Australia have lost four straight, the latest 12–15 to Scotland at Murrayfield. Les Kiss has changed five of his pack and benched Fraser McReight, the current John Eales Medalist, for Carlo Tizzano. The backline that lost in Edinburgh stays as it was.

Steve Tandy has gone back to the XV that beat Japan. Aaron Wainwright is fit again after missing the New Zealand win, and Josh Adams is back after being rested. Win by 16 or more and Wales go above Australia into eighth in the world.
Australia's last win, in September, was 42–38 over South Africa. South Africa beat Wales 43–0 in July. Form is less transitive than it looks.
